title: Singular adjective agreement in partitive
summary: Before a singular partitive noun, put the adjective in singular partitive too: Etsin pientä kirjaa. — I am looking for a small book.
objectives: Match an adjective to a singular partitive noun inside a phrase.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Match an adjective to a singular partitive noun inside a phrase.
The adjective stands before the noun. Both are singular partitive, although their endings can look different. The noun form is provided; choose the matching adjective.
The complete adjective alternatives are shown. Forming a new adjective stem is not an additional task.
keyPoints: An adjective directly describing this singular partitive noun also takes singular partitive. Agreement means matching the noun’s case and number.

sections.title: A familiar greeting
paragraphs: When greeting someone in the morning, Hyvää huomenta! means “Good morning!”. Learn this as a fixed expression; hyvää visibly uses the same adjective form.
keyPoints: A fixed greeting can contain a familiar partitive adjective.

examples.english: I am looking for a big car.
steps: An adjective directly describing this singular partitive noun also takes singular partitive. Agreement means matching the noun’s case and number.
Etsin means “I am looking for” and works as the verb. etsin comes from etsiä: etsi- + -n.
isoa means “big” and works as the singular partitive adjective agreeing with the following noun. Keep iso and add -a: iso + a = isoa.
autoa means “car” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Add -a to auto: autoa. The ending is selected from the word’s back vowels.

examples.english: I am looking for a small book.
steps: An adjective directly describing this singular partitive noun also takes singular partitive. Agreement means matching the noun’s case and number.
Etsin means “I am looking for” and works as the verb. etsin comes from etsiä: etsi- + -n.
pientä means “small” and works as the singular partitive adjective agreeing with the following noun. pieni uses pien- + -tä = pientä.
kirjaa means “book” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep kirja and add -a: kirja + a = kirjaa.

examples.english: I am looking for a new bus.
steps: An adjective directly describing this singular partitive noun also takes singular partitive. Agreement means matching the noun’s case and number.
Etsin means “I am looking for” and works as the verb. etsin comes from etsiä: etsi- + -n.
uutta means “new” and works as the singular partitive adjective agreeing with the following noun. uusi uses uut- + -ta, written uutta; keep the long uu.
bussia means “bus” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep bussi and add -a: bussi + a = bussia.
An adjective directly describing this singular partitive noun also takes singular partitive. Agreement means matching the noun’s case and number.
Juon means “I drink” and works as the verb. juon comes from juoda: juo- + -n.
hyvää means “good” and works as the singular partitive adjective agreeing with the following noun. Keep hyvä and add -ä: hyvä + ä = hyvää.
kahvia means “coffee” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. This i-word keeps i: kahvi + a = kahvia. The back vowel a determines the ending.

commonMistakes: Do not leave the adjective in its dictionary form beside a partitive noun.
Agreement means the same case and number, not necessarily identical final letters.
